weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 18 at 1:41PM EST until November 22 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to
10 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Southeast Georgia and Northeast Florida Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Sunday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

dangerous surf conditions.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 20 at 12:58AM EST until November 22 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and
rough surf. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
5 to 12 feet in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Up to 3.0 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties. * WHEN...From 4 AM Saturday to 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM Saturday, 2.1 ft above normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at 8:48 AM Sunday, 2.3 ft above normal (8.1 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.9 ft above normal (8.7 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 3.0 ft above normal (8.8 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

location.region: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast

Francisco Bay, respectively.

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 8. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 7 AM EST Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.0 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. High surf will likely continue much of next week, peaking on Wednesday and Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches, Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches, Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Additional products will likely be needed into Friday.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 1.75 to 2.00 feet above ground level is possible along shorelines and low-lying coastal areas of Grays Harbor County. Inundation along the northern coast may be around 2.30 to 2.60 feet above ground level. * WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County Coast zones. * WHEN...From 7 AM to 3 PM PST Sunday. * IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road closures expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Increasing waves along the Pacific coast may also increase water levels around high tide Sunday morning. While impacts may be limited on Sunday, additional rounds of coastal flooding will be expected during additional high tides early next week.

location.region: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 21 at 1:40PM PST until November 22 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 1.75 to
2.00 feet above ground level is possible along shorelines and
low-lying coastal areas of Grays Harbor County. Inundation
along the northern coast may be around 2.30 to 2.60 feet above
ground level.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

* WHEN...From 7 AM to 3 PM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is
expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of
parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road
closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Increasing waves along the Pacific coast
may also increase water levels around high tide Sunday morning.
While impacts may be limited on Sunday, additional rounds of
coastal flooding will be expected during additional high tides
early next week.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.
weather.areaDesc: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...Life-threatening rip current. * WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo. * WHEN...Through 6 AM AST Sunday. * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to return to safety.

location.region: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 21 at 4:23PM AST until November 22 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
weather.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo.

* WHEN...Through 6 AM AST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
weather.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.
weather.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity

events.description: The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart County, in effect from 6 PM Saturday November 21st to 10 AM EST Sunday November 22nd. A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor exposure. Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as much as possible. For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at: http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 21 at 2:45AM EST until November 22 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...Through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South Washington Coast. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Monday night through late Thursday night. * IMPACTS...Major flooding, up to two foot above ground level, during high tides is possible along the immediate coast as well as low lying areas near bays, sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding is expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and property. A Coastal Flood Watch means that conditions favorable for flooding are expected to develop. Coastal residents should be alert for later statements or warnings, and take action to protect property.

events.description: * WHAT...Up to 2.8 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Pacific Ocean Coast. * WHEN...Through 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.0 ft above normal (7.8 ft MLLW) at 8:48 AM Sunday, 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

weather.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 22 at 12:27AM CST by NWS Norman OK
weather.description:
At 1226 AM CST, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms along
a line extending from 6 miles east of Arapaho to 3 miles east of
Cordell to 6 miles west of Boone. Movement was east at 45 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Weatherford, Clinton, Cordell, Carnegie, Apache, Cyril, Hydro,
Arapaho, Mountain View, Fort Cobb, Dill City, Corn, Custer City,
Eakly, Gotebo, Bessie, Rocky, Colony, Cloud Chief, and Boone.
weather.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with these storms.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

events.title: Air Quality Alert
events.description: The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory, IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 AM EST THIS MORNING. A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM2.5 has been issued. Fine particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor exposure. Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as much as possible. For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at: http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

events.description: * WHAT...Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf may cause major flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to 2.5 to 3 feet of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways during the highest tides if storm impacts such as strong southerly winds and large surf arrive during high tide periods. * WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 11 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Monday morning through Thursday afternoon. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur.

location.region: Northern Coastal Humboldt

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 21 at 9:39PM PST until November 22 at 11:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large
surf may cause major flooding in low lying areas along the
Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to 2.5 to 3 feet of saltwater
inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways during the highest tides
if storm impacts such as strong southerly winds and large surf
arrive during high tide periods.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 11 AM PST
Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Monday morning
through Thursday afternoon. Saltwater inundation will be
possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
Some shoreline erosion may occur.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that flooding is possible but not
imminent. Coastal residents in the watch area should begin
preparations for rising water and take appropriate action to
protect life and property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.
weather.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected. * WHERE...East facing reefs of the Marianas. * WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A building trade-wind swell will produce a high risk of rip currents along east facing reefs. Surf and the rip current risk will also be elevated along north facing reefs, but remain just below High Surf Advisory and High Rip Current Risk levels.

location.region: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 22 at 3:37PM ChST until November 26 at 3:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...East facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A building trade-wind swell will produce a
high risk of rip currents along east facing reefs. Surf and the rip
current risk will also be elevated along north facing reefs, but
remain just below High Surf Advisory and High Rip Current Risk
levels.
weather.instruction:
Rip currents will be life threatening. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 1.75 to 2.00 feet above ground level is possible along shorelines and low-lying coastal areas of Grays Harbor County. Inundation along the northern coast may be around 2.30 to 2.60 feet above ground level. * WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County Coast zones. * WHEN...From 7 AM to 3 PM PST Sunday. * IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road closures expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Increasing waves along the Pacific coast may also increase water levels around high tide Sunday morning. While impacts may be limited on Sunday, additional rounds of coastal flooding will be expected during additional high tides early next week.

location.region: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 21 at 8:17PM PST until November 22 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 1.75 to
2.00 feet above ground level is possible along shorelines and
low-lying coastal areas of Grays Harbor County. Inundation
along the northern coast may be around 2.30 to 2.60 feet above
ground level.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

* WHEN...From 7 AM to 3 PM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is
expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of
parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road
closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Increasing waves along the Pacific coast
may also increase water levels around high tide Sunday morning.
While impacts may be limited on Sunday, additional rounds of
coastal flooding will be expected during additional high tides
early next week.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tides between about 730 AM and 930 AM. * WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Elevated to high surf is expected much of the week, peaking on Wednesday and Thursday. Additional products will likely be needed into Friday.

events.title: Air Quality Alert
events.description: The officials at the Office of Sustainability for the City of Indianapolis have called for a Knozone Action Day, IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 AM EST SUNDAY. A Knozone Action day means that a combination of high temperatures, light winds, and other factors are expected to produce conditions where high levels of ozone emissions may exceed federally mandated standards. Fine particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor exposure. Here are some recommended actions that the public can take: * Walk, bike, carpool or use public transportation. * Avoid using the drive-through and combine errands into one trip. * Avoid refueling your vehicle or using gasoline-powered lawn equipment until after 7pm. * Turn off your engine when idling for more than 30 seconds. * Conserve energy by turning off lights or setting the air conditioner to 75 degrees or above. For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at: http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet, likely re-breaking the all time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3- 5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday. Uncertainty remains in exact surf heights at this time, but look to be 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches.

events.description: * WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents. * WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo. * WHEN...Through 6 AM AST Sunday. * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to return to safety.

location.region: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 21 at 9:46PM AST until November 22 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
weather.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo.

* WHEN...Through 6 AM AST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
weather.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.
